name: Suspicious Parent-Child Process Relationships
hypothesis: If an attacker used a phishing document to execute code, we expect to see Office applications (Word, Excel) spawning unusual child processes like PowerShell or cmd.exe.

name: LOLBin Abuse for Tool Download
hypothesis: Attackers living off the land use legitimate Windows binaries (certutil, bitsadmin, mshta) to download malicious files, avoiding AV detection.
mitre: T1105 - Ingress Tool Transfer via LOLBin

name: Lateral Movement via NTLM Authentication
hypothesis: An attacker who has stolen NTLM hashes will authenticate to multiple hosts in quick succession using pass-the-hash. We look for one account logging into 3+ hosts via NTLM within a short window.

name: Process Masquerading in User-Writable Paths
hypothesis: Malware often copies itself to user-writable locations using the name of a legitimate Windows process (svchost.exe, lsass.exe) to blend in.

name: Outbound Connections from Non-Browser Processes
hypothesis: Implants and beacons make direct outbound connections from unusual processes (PowerShell, cmd.exe, certutil). Normal user workstations should only have browsers making outbound HTTPS connections.
